Just weeks after announcing a price hike for Apple Music, Apple today announced that Apple TV is also getting a price increase. Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that the Apple TV monthly fee will rise from US$12.99 to US$14.99.

The individual plan of Apple One will also see a price increase.

Apple TV and Apple One both raise prices

Below are the details of the price increase:

  • Apple TV (monthly): US$14.99 (originally US$12.99)
  • Apple TV (annual): US$119 (originally US$99)
  • Apple One Individual Plan: US$21.95 (originally US$19.95)

Prices for other Apple One plans remain unchanged. When Apple raised Apple Music prices last month, it also raised the Apple One Family Plan and Apple One Premier Plan, but did not raise the Individual Plan at that time.

New charges take effect today for new subscribers. Apple said existing subscribers will be notified approximately one month before the price increase takes effect.

The last time Apple raised Apple TV prices was in August 2025, when the monthly fee was raised from US$9.99 to US$12.99. At that time, the annual plan and Apple One bundle prices were not adjusted.

Apple has significantly expanded the Apple TV content lineup over the past year. In October last year, Apple announced an agreement with F1, becoming its exclusive broadcast partner in the United States. F1 race streaming is now included in the standard Apple TV subscription at no additional cost.

Earlier this year, Apple also added Major League Soccer (MLS) matches to Apple TV at no additional cost. Previously, MLS required a separate subscription to MLS Season Pass.

Apple has also benefited from the recent strong performance of several titles, including the fourth season of "Ted Lasso." Apple TV today also premieres the second season of "Dark Matter." The sixth season of "Slow Horses" will premiere on September 16.

What do you think of Apple TV's new pricing? Is US$14.99 reasonable given the content Apple TV offers? Feel free to tell us in the comments section.
